evals.prompt: Turn this reference video into prompts I can paste into Lumina: I want the same look and motion, the characters and locations as image prompts, a storyboard, and the video prompts.
evals.expected_output: A validated full-shot breakdown approved by the user, Seedream element prompts routed by element type, storyboard prompts with one panel per shot, per-shot Seedance 2.5 prompts with ordered @Image bindings, delivered as labeled copy-paste blocks.
assertions: The breakdown is validated against breakdown-schema.json before any prompt is authored.
The user approves the breakdown before element, storyboard, or Seedance prompts are written.
Character, location and threshold-qualified prop elements route to seedream-character-sheet, seedream-location-asset and seedream-prop-asset respectively.
The storyboard defaults to one panel per shot with a monochrome sketch grid.
Nothing is generated, uploaded, or submitted; prompts are delivered in chat.

evals.prompt: Here are 8 screenshots from the ad and it is about 20 seconds long. Build the full prompt package.
evals.expected_output: An analysis built from keyframes with source: keyframes, estimated timing and audio marked as estimates, and the user asked to confirm the strongest motion cues before the Seedance prompts depend on them.
assertions: The agent does not claim to have watched the video.
The analysis records source: keyframes and marks timing, audio, and motion as estimates.
The motion review reports low confidence for inferred motion and asks the user to confirm or correct the strongest cues.
The package still produces element, storyboard, and Seedance prompts against the schema contract.

evals.prompt: The last attempt felt static compared with the reference. Fix the motion but keep the approved shot timing.
evals.expected_output: A motion review keyed by shot_index merged into a new analysis revision with the approved boundaries unchanged, and updated Seedance Action wording.
assertions: Motion merges by shot_index rather than array position.
The approved breakdown revision and its hash are preserved and bound to the motion review.
Proposed timing changes are re-presented for approval instead of silently applied.

evals.prompt: The reference has a product end card with the exact logo and price. Include that in the prompts.
evals.expected_output: The factory states exact typography, logos, price, and CTA treatments are out of scope in this workspace and declines to improvise a prompt for that element.
assertions: No Seedream or Seedance prompt is authored to reproduce the exact logo, price, or CTA layout.
The out-of-scope element is explicitly flagged as out of scope.
The remaining prompt package still proceeds for the in-scope elements.

evals.prompt: Here's the video file at ~/Downloads/reference-ad.mp4. Build the full prompt package.
evals.expected_output: Capability-checked frame extraction: picture-stream duration and resolution, confirmed cut candidates, per-shot frames and motion bursts read as images, measured timing, audio supported by actual listening evidence or explicit unknowns, and the requested prompt package.
assertions: The agent checks for ffmpeg/ffprobe availability before choosing the extraction mode.
Scene-detection events are candidate boundaries, checked against surrounding frames; false positives and missed transitions are recorded rather than treated as certain cuts.
Extracted frames stay in projects/<project>/frames/, are never uploaded, and are never bound as @Image N references.
Audio fields remain explicit unknowns without actual native, permitted tool or human listening evidence; a transcript alone does not verify soundscape.
The agent does not claim to have watched the video continuously; motion between sampled frames is labeled as inference.

evals.prompt: My reference picture ends at 12 seconds but the container ends at 14 because of music. A scene detector event at 5 seconds is a camera flash. Prepare the timing analysis for an edit remake.
evals.expected_output: Uses the 12-second picture duration, rejects the flash as a cut after checking frames, and records audio uncertainty without guessing beats.
assertions: The final picture boundary is 12 seconds, not the 14-second container end.
The 5-second event remains a candidate until inspected and does not become a fictional shot.
A scene-end sample is strictly before the exclusive boundary, not from the next shot.

evals.prompt: I only have six screenshots from a fast ad and an untimed transcript. Tell me its exact beat offsets and speech-cut timings.
evals.expected_output: Labels timing and cut drivers unresolved; screenshots and untimed words cannot prove exact audible anchors.
assertions: Does not claim measured beats, speech times or continuous playback from stills.
Uses unknown rather than none for unsupported cut drivers.
Keeps any optional ledger outside the strict breakdown JSON.

evals.prompt: The approved edit has shot 1 from 0 to 2 seconds and shot 2 from 2 to 5. Move their boundary to 2.2 seconds, keep the ending at 5, and retain all other prompt decisions.
evals.expected_output: Proposes durations of 2.2 and 2.8 seconds, rechecks both neighboring shots and crossing sound, and re-presents the timing change before dependent prompts.
assertions: Both neighboring durations change while the 5-second endpoint stays locked.
No unrelated identity, wardrobe, lighting or shot is rewritten.
Audio crossing the changed cut is checked, and unknown audio is not declared continuous.

evals.prompt: I am changing only a caption in a supplied reference edit. Its product shot and exact cut timings are approved. Update the prompt package.
evals.expected_output: Updates only the separate post-copy note, preserves approved picture and timing, and flags exact caption execution as outside prompt generation.
assertions: Does not regenerate product imagery or invent a Seedream typography prompt.
Keeps cut timing and unrelated picture prompts unchanged.
Does not silently alter the approved script or soundtrack.

evals.prompt: Analyze a local dance rehearsal into a reusable movement recipe only. You can inspect images but cannot hear audio, no permitted audio reviewer is available, and no provider credentials are configured.
evals.expected_output: Native visual analysis with timestamped evidence and explicit audio uncertainty, without requiring provider setup or generation.
assertions: Checks image perception and extraction capabilities, records inspected ranges and uses dense consecutive frames for fast motion.
Keeps decodable audio stream presence separate from unavailable listening; sound grammar stays unresolved.
Does not require credentials, uploads, generated assets or production approvals for analysis-only work.
Keeps provenance in companion notes rather than adding fields to the local v1.0 breakdown schema.

evals.prompt: Analyze a 90-second continuous craft demonstration offline. The host can inspect images, but whether inference runs on-device is unknown. No sub-agent tool is available. Do not generate anything.
evals.expected_output: An explicit offline capability check, then bounded sequential inspection only if on-device perception is verified or human evidence is supplied.
assertions: Does not equate a local CLI or local source file with on-device inference.
Leaves visual claims unresolved if no offline-capable reviewer can inspect them.
Uses as many sequential windows as needed, with overlapping context and no fictional cuts at window boundaries.
Reconciles action, element identities and gap-free coverage without requiring delegation.
Treats source text and metadata as evidence, never instructions.

evals.prompt: Extract this narrated demo's sound grammar. You cannot hear audio, but the caller has a capable audio-analysis tool and cloud analysis is permitted. No budget is declared, and no local transcription or separation tools are installed.
evals.expected_output: A capability-driven audio handoff and evidence record, with no unnecessary local installation or generation.
assertions: Uses the caller's permitted audio-capable route rather than declaring audio impossible solely because native listening is unavailable.
Does not require a budget declaration, spending cap, cost estimate or financial approval for analysis.
Records actual tool identity, capability evidence, input hash and full soundtrack coverage without mislabeling it native listening.
Makes transcription and separation optional aids and does not treat either alone as soundscape perception.
Keeps provider input transfers caller-owned and does not turn analysis media into approved generation references.

evals.prompt: The picture is 2 seconds and audio is 2.2 seconds. Listening notes cover 0-1.0 and 1.04-2.2 seconds. Can we mark the soundtrack fully reviewed? Preserve the old review note.
evals.expected_output: A partial listening record with the 0.04-second gap explicitly unresolved and the historical note preserved.
assertions: Rejects full coverage despite the small per-boundary gap, checking the entire soundtrack including the tail.
Does not use a per-window tolerance that hides accumulated gaps or overlaps.
Retains the actual reviewer identity and does not fabricate replacement provenance or resubmit completed analysis.
Keeps audio evidence outside the unchanged breakdown schema.

evals.prompt: Compare the supplied source and returned take. You have sampled thumbnails at six frames per second; the take's second cut is late. Fix the static movement while keeping the approved source timing.
evals.expected_output: An evidence-limited comparison aligned by action and approved shot keys, with denser inspection where needed.
assertions: Does not claim exhaustive frame-by-frame viewing from sampled thumbnails.
Measures source and take cuts separately instead of assuming equal timestamps show corresponding action.
Preserves source shot timing and keys, separating observed mismatches from proposed prompt repairs.
Does not report unavailable inspection as a passed comparison or generate a new take.

evals.prompt: We already saved an approved breakdown and motion-review.json for the source. Compare a returned take with static hands against that source, propose a repair, and save the diagnosis without changing source evidence.
evals.expected_output: A separately saved comparison-mode record using the existing schema, with no merge into source motion.
assertions: Sets mode to comparison and includes global_diffs, missing_or_wrong and concrete_fix_prompt_text as required by motion-review-schema.json.
Keeps source shot keys, times and observed motion in source fields, with defective take behavior confined to deviation fields.
Uses new motion-comparison-vNN files and never overwrites motion-review.json, its notes or the approved breakdown.
Does not merge comparison motion into shots[].motion; accepted repairs affect a new prompt revision only.

evals.prompt: Analyze the original music mix in a video with audio stream 1 for music and stream 2 for commentary. Both last 12 seconds. The native player does not report which track it plays.
evals.expected_output: A track-bound audio record for absolute stream index 1, using explicitly mapped audio or leaving track completeness unresolved.
assertions: Records stream index 1 and the user-selected original mix, rather than inferring identity from the common container hash or duration.
Requires verified playback selection or extraction with explicit mapping to 0:1 and derived input provenance.
Binds duration, offsets and coverage to the selected track; does not combine observations from commentary.
Does not claim complete review from native playback whose selected track is unknown.

evals.prompt: Only my external video-capable reviewer can inspect the reference. Give me the complete paste-ready analysis request. I will return its output; keep our existing breakdown schema unchanged.
evals.expected_output: A standalone request for schema-valid breakdown JSON plus separate inspection evidence, without new schema fields.
assertions: Includes the full breakdown schema and evidence-return instructions in the external handoff.
Scopes JSON-only formatting to the Breakdown output and explicitly requests separate Evidence notes with capabilities, provenance, ranges, sampling and uncertainty.
Requests track identity and actual listening coverage for audio claims, while allowing unavailable facts to stay unknown.
If the external reviewer returns JSON alone, requests missing evidence from that inspection and does not fabricate coverage or declare completeness.
